subject: Walkling Court Redevelopment Project
overview: The committee received a status update on the $117 million Walkling Court redevelopment, which proposes replacing 144 aging units with 238 deeply affordable senior and family apartments. The update was received and placed on file following discussions on funding mechanisms, railway noise mitigation, and neighborhood infrastructure impacts.

items.title: Update on Saltonstall Building Renovation
items.summary: Jeffrey Driscoll reported that the $105 million Saltonstall project is currently undergoing a complete gut renovation and facade replacement to modernize 200 units and add 22 new units.

items.title: Walkling Court Redevelopment Presentation
items.summary: Gabe Ciccariello detailed a plan to replace nine 1960s-era walk-up buildings with elevator-accessible mid-rise structures and townhomes for seniors and families.

items.title: Funding and Voucher Program Conversion
items.summary: Margaret Moran explained the financial transition to a federal project-based voucher model intended to secure $60 million in low-income housing tax credits.

items.title: Design and Infrastructure Discussion
items.summary: Councilors questioned representatives about sound attenuation for adjacent train traffic, traffic calming for the proposed through-street, and parking ratios for the new development.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Community members shared testimony regarding the potential loss of mature trees and traffic safety at the North Street bridge, while current residents emphasized the urgent need for elevators and accessible housing.
